rules.title: Source-of-lawful-income discrimination ban (NJ Law Against Discrimination)
rules.requirement: The NJ Law Against Discrimination prohibits housing discrimination based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent or mortgage payment. A landlord cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder the right to rent solely because of that income source.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, business or residential, except the listed exemptions (owner-occupied two-family unit, room rentals in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling, religious organization preference).
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt: rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit as a residence; rental of rooms by the owner or occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Religious organizations may give preference to persons of the same religion.

rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the owner lives in the other unit; rental of a room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference for persons of the same religion in sale, lease or rental.
rules.quoted_span:
This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
